deciles.definition: pandas.qcut(values, q=10, duplicates='drop') on the evaluated rows' values, as feature_research.model_training.rf.lift_analysis.compute_lift forms them (exact edges from retbins; intervals (lo, hi], the first including its lower edge). Rows with equal values always share a decile, so deciles of these clustered encodings hold unequal row counts. In-sample deciles: edges from the in-sample values. Out-of-fold deciles: edges from the pooled out-of-fold values, applied unchanged to each fold's held-out rows (each fold's lift against that fold's base rate).

encoder_comparison.definition:
Three evaluations per bin with the frozen cut points, each lift against the
base rate of the rows it evaluates:

``in_sample``  the engineer fitted on all training rows, on those rows;
``fold_fit``   each fold's engineer on its own fit rows (pairs (fold, row):
               every training row appears in four fits);
``oof``        each fold's engineer on its held-out rows (PR 39).

Two descriptive contrasts, named for what they compute, add up to
``oof_minus_in_sample``:

``fold_fit_minus_in_sample``  different encoders (five fold fits against the
                              all-rows fit), each evaluated on the rows that
                              built it;
``heldout_minus_fold_fit``    the same five encoders, evaluated on different
                              rows (held-out against fit rows), pooled.

Neither isolates a cause. ``heldout_minus_fold_fit`` is not the effect of a
row's own label: within a fold the held-out and fit rows differ in
composition, and fold-level differences of opposite sign cancel in the pool
(``per_fold`` gives them). The direct evidence of what an encoder does is
which macro states it assigns to each bin (``focal_assignments``,
``straddling_states``) and which rows change bin (``migration``).

findings.explanation: Encoder behaviour at cuts that sit inside the ranges whole macro states take across fits. NSD and ECI are functions of the macro state (euribor3m, nr.employed, emp.var.rate), so all rows of a state cross a cut together. Fold 0's encoder assigns nsd_elevated to 7 states of 2009-05 (prevalence 0.088), which are nsd_warm in sample and under every other fold's encoder, and assigns nsd_hot to all 50 states of the in-sample bin (2009-06, 2009-07, 2009-08). Every row that enters or leaves the bin between the in-sample and out-of-fold encoders is a fold-0 row. Its 374 held-out bin rows have 0.62x, and that encoder's own fit rows in the bin 1.01x; the other folds have 2.82-3.36x, and without fold 0 the pooled lift is 3.15x. The fold encoders' pooled lift on their own fit rows (2.509x) is close to the out-of-fold 2.486x, against 3.126x in sample; the held-out-minus-fit contrast (-0.022) pools per-fold differences from -0.39 to +0.29 and does not isolate a row's own label. Historically the figures 1.04-1.43x were two deciles (the 1.04x one lies in nsd_warm), and the bin's own lift at lock time was 1.25x on 10.7% of rows, against 4.0% in sample on the training rows: the same cut selected a different set of states.

focal_assignments.definition:
Row- and state-level facts the focal findings state, each checked on row
masks or on the per-state, per-encoder assignments (``state_values``), not
on matching counts or lifts.

``eci_hot``       the in-sample bin split by whether a row's contact period is
                  below the base rate; whether the below-base rows are exactly
                  the rows of a set of macro states; each such state's bin
                  under each of the six encoders; whether the out-of-fold
                  bin's below-base rows are the same rows; whether the
                  in-sample top decile is exactly the bin's other rows.
``nsd_elevated``  for the fold with the lowest out-of-fold lift: the states its
                  encoder assigns to the bin, their periods and in-sample bins,
                  and the bins it assigns to the in-sample bin's states; the
                  other encoders' bins for those states; the folds of every row
                  that enters or leaves the bin between the in-sample and the
                  out-of-fold encoders.

limits: The historical figures were computed on all 41,188 rows (the rows now in the test split among them) with an encoder fitted on those rows. They are transcribed and Git-verified, never recomputed (G7), so the historical-to-training difference combines population, fit size and reference draw (legacy np.random against np.random.default_rng), which the training side cannot separate.

Every comparison here uses random folds. All encoders, in sample and out of fold, use labels of later contacts (Commit 3: about 47% of the NSD and 52% of the ECI label mass or influence). The mean shares are similar in sample and out of fold, but similar means can come from different contributing labels and give different encoded values. A past-only NSD or ECI is not built (Commit 3, Step 3B section 5), so the effect of look-ahead on these lifts, and on the gaps between them, is unresolved.

The two encoder contrasts are descriptive. fold_fit_minus_in_sample changes the encoders and the weighting of rows at once; heldout_minus_fold_fit compares the same encoders on different rows, so fold composition and the cancellation of per-fold differences affect it. Neither isolates a row's own label.

Period-standardized ratios near 1 show that period mix reproduces a bin's aggregate subscriber count; within-period differences can cancel in them (the absolute-deviation share and the within-period ratios are reported beside them).
The six training-side encoders differ in their fit rows' labels and in their 5,000-row KDE reference draw at once; which of the two moves the NSD states across a cut is not separated.

The frozen cut points are constants chosen with all labels (PR 39 limitation). No threshold is evaluated as a candidate for adoption here: the historical edges are described, not compared under registered criteria. Fold-fitted procedures, registered criteria and candidate comparisons are Step 4B.
Wilson intervals cover binomial sampling of the evaluated rows only (WILSON_ESTIMAND); fold-to-fold encoder variation is shown by the per-fold tables, not by the intervals.
Fold-fit tables pool (fold, fit row) pairs: each training row counts four times.

periods.definition:
Per bin and contact period: rows, positives, rate, lift and the
within-period ratio (bin rate / period rate), in sample and out of fold
(with each fold's rows). Per bin (``standardized``):

``observed_over_expected``       observed / expected subscribers, expected =
                                 sum over periods of the bin's rows x the
                                 period's rate (all training rows). Near 1, the
                                 period mix reproduces the bin's aggregate
                                 subscriber count; within-period differences
                                 of opposite sign can cancel in it;
``abs_deviation_over_expected``  sum over periods of |observed - expected| /
                                 expected: the within-period differences
                                 without cancellation;
``within_period_ratio_min/max``  over the bin's periods with at least
                                 ``PERIOD_MIN_ROWS`` rows in it;
``shared_periods``               the bin's periods that also have rows in
                                 another bin of its family (same kind); with
                                 none, the bin is a union of whole periods and
                                 its ratio is 1 by construction.

support.estimand: lift = the bin's subscription rate on the evaluated rows / the base rate of the same rows (pooled: all evaluated rows; per fold: that fold's rows). lift_wilson95 = the Wilson 95% interval of the bin's rate (stage2_binning.evidence.wilson) divided by that base rate. It covers binomial sampling of the evaluated rows only: the base rate, the fitted encoders and the cut points are held fixed, so it does not cover fold-to-fold encoder variation, and pooled out-of-fold rows, which come from five encoders, are treated as one sample. Tables over (fold, fit row) pairs count each training row four times; their pooled intervals are omitted.
